title: Contrasting misinformation and real-information dissemination network structures on social media during a health emergency (Spanish translation: Comparacion de las estructuras de difusion de informacion erronea y veridica en las redes sociales durante una emergencia de salud publica)
screen_reason: The paper systematically reviewed the 5,000 most-retweeted English-language Zika tweets of 2016 and identified 400 of them as containing misinformation against an evidence-based definition - an exact share of items in a defined sample judged false against an external ground truth, i.e. CONTENT prevalence with a denominator (400/5,000 = 8.0%). The rest of the paper is a network-structure comparison (nine metrics) that yields no further shares.

estimates.measure_type: % of the 5,000 most-retweeted English-language Zika tweets of 2016 that were judged to contain misinformation
estimates.value_raw: "De los 5 000 tuits sobre el zika mas retuiteados en el 2016, detectamos un total de 400 que contenian informacion erronea" [English: 'Of the 5,000 most-retweeted Zika tweets of 2016, we detected a total of 400 that contained misinformation'] = 400/5,000 = 8.0%; only 266 of the 400 had enough metadata to reconstruct a retweet network
estimates.denominator: The 5,000 most-retweeted original English-language Zika tweets of 2016 (each retweeted at least 50 times), ranked from a full-year corpus of 3.7 million English Zika tweets and retweets collected through the Gnip API with the keyword 'zika'
estimates.definition: The information contained in the tweet was not evidence-based, assessed against peer-reviewed journal articles and conference proceedings, reports and statistics from official and health agencies (e.g. CDC, WHO) and fact-checking websites
estimates.misinfo_def: "establecimos una definicion operativa de 'informacion erronea', es decir, que la informacion contenida en el tuit no estuviese basada en evidencia" [English: 'we established an operational definition of "misinformation", namely that the information contained in the tweet was not based on evidence']
estimates.source_quote: De los 5 000 tuits sobre el zika más retuiteados en el 2016, detectamos un total de 400 que contenían información errónea y los verificamos.
estimates.page_loc: RESULTADOS, first paragraph, p. 3 (Rev Panam Salud Publica 2021;45:e61); Methods, 'Deteccion de informacion erronea y equiparacion con informacion veridica', p. 2; English abstract (Am J Public Health 2020;110:S340-S347)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: The authors systematically reviewed all 5,000 tweets and applied their own evidence-based operational definition, validating each tweet against peer-reviewed journal articles and conference proceedings, reports and statistics from official and health agencies (CDC, WHO) and fact-checking websites. The detailed application of the definition, the reliability guarantee and worked examples are relegated to Appendix A, which is NOT part of this text, so no inter-coder reliability statistic can be recorded. The authors explicitly note that the evidence base shifts over time (they cite The Economist tweeting in December 2016 that Zika was harmless to adults, which would not have counted as misinformation earlier in 2016).
estimates.moderator_quote: "Clasificamos todos los tuits originales sobre el zika segun el numero de veces que fueron retuiteados, de mayor a menor. Despues de esta clasificacion descendente, seleccionamos los 5 000 tuits mas retuiteados como muestra." [English: 'We ranked all original Zika tweets by the number of times they were retweeted, from highest to lowest. After this descending ranking, we selected the 5,000 most-retweeted tweets as our sample.'] ; "Consideramos que un tuit era popular si se retuiteaba al menos 50 veces." [English: 'We considered a tweet popular if it was retweeted at least 50 times.']
estimates.notes: ENGLISH TRANSLATION of source_quote (kept verbatim in Spanish so it can be located in the text file): 'Of the 5,000 most-retweeted Zika tweets of 2016, we detected a total of 400 that contained misinformation and verified them.' The surrounding sentences read: 'Our sample contains about 5,000 tweets above that figure. ... Of these, 266 contained enough metadata to reconstruct the dissemination network.' The percentage is not printed; it is an exact part/whole share from two verbatim counts with the same denominator (400/5,000), permitted by R8. KEY DENOMINATOR CAVEAT: the denominator is a RANK-TRUNCATED set - the top 5,000 most-retweeted original Zika tweets, each with at least 50 retweets, out of 3.7 million English Zika tweets and retweets - hence denom_selection=curated. This is therefore the misinformation share among the most VIRAL Zika tweets, not among all Zika tweets, and it is not comparable to corpus-wide prevalence figures. Do NOT use 266/5,000 (5.3%): the 266 are only those misinformation tweets whose metadata survived (accounts banned, content deleted, or authors retracting), and that number is an analytic subset for network reconstruction, not a prevalence. breadth coded 'false'; note the operational definition ('not based on evidence') is arguably broader and could be read as 'misleading'. This text is the Pan American Health Organization's official Spanish translation of the English original (Am J Public Health 2020;110:S340-S347); the publisher states the English version prevails in case of discrepancy. The English abstract appended to the file matches the Spanish numbers (266 misinformation and 458 real-information tweets).

missed_or_uncertain: 1) Verified-account shares: "el porcentaje de usuarios verificados es mas alto que en el grupo de informacion veridica (2% frente al 1,2%)" [English: 'the percentage of verified users is higher in the real-information group than in the misinformation group (2% vs 1.2%)']. Not extracted: this is the share of verified ACCOUNTS within each group, not a share of misinformation, and no denominator counts are given. 2) "alrededor del 30% de los tuits con informacion erronea tenian un mismo nodo retuiteado al menos dos veces, cifra sustancialmente mas alta que en el grupo de informacion veridica (<10%)" [English: 'around 30% of misinformation tweets had the same node retweeting at least twice, substantially higher than in the real-information group (<10%)'] - a network-structure property computed inside each group, not a misinformation prevalence. 3) The 458 comparable real-information tweets are a MATCHED comparison group selected on posting date and retweet count, not a random sample, so 266/(266+458) is meaningless as a prevalence and was not computed. 4) All nine network metrics (Cuadro 1: diameter, Wiener index, density, size, reach, virality, modularity, betweenness, out-degree) are distributions and means, not shares; the same is true of the retweet-timing results (T50 = 334 vs 448 min, T90 = 2,580 vs 1,795 min, T95 = 4,739 vs 2,824 min, T100 = 34,869 vs 22,340 min). 5) No CONCENTRATION row is possible: the paper reports maximum out-degree and betweenness centrality scores per network but never states a top group as a % of users together with their % of retweets, so R1 cannot be met. 6) Appendices A-C (definition application, reliability, network algorithm) are not in this text, so the coding reliability of the misinformation labels is unverifiable here.

rob.design: Observational Twitter study. Full-year sampling frame: all English-language tweets and retweets containing the keyword 'zika' posted between 1 January and 31 December 2016, collected via the Gnip API (3.7 million), which the authors describe as the complete English Zika conversation on Twitter for that year. Original tweets were ranked by retweet count and the top 5,000 (each with at least 50 retweets) were systematically reviewed by the authors against an evidence-based operational definition of misinformation, validated with peer-reviewed literature, CDC/WHO reports and statistics, and fact-checking websites; 400 misinformation tweets were identified and verified. A comparison group of 458 real-information tweets was matched on posting date and retweet count, deliberately NOT one-to-one, to avoid selection bias. Retweet networks were reconstructed for 266 misinformation tweets (the rest lacked metadata because accounts were banned, content deleted or posts retracted) using an inference algorithm based on posting time and friend/follower relations, since Twitter does not publish who retweets whom. Nine network metrics were compared with two-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests; analysis in Python 3.7.3 and R 3.5.0. Threats: no inter-coder reliability reported in this text (Appendix A only); labels depend on the evidence base at the time; the misinformation set survives a metadata-availability filter (400 -> 266) that is plausibly correlated with platform enforcement; English-only; results describe only the most viral tweets.
rob.item6_quote: A continuacion, establecimos una definicion operativa de "informacion erronea", es decir, que la informacion contenida en el tuit no estuviese basada en evidencia. Para evaluar la validez de un tuit, utilizamos articulos de revistas especializadas y actas de congresos con revision externa, informes y estadisticas de organismos oficiales y de salud (p. ej., los Centros para el Control y la Prevencion de Enfermedades y la OMS) y sitios web de verificacion de datos. [English: 'Next, we established an operational definition of "misinformation", namely that the information contained in the tweet was not based on evidence. To assess the validity of a tweet we used peer-reviewed journal articles and conference proceedings, reports and statistics from official and health agencies (e.g. the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the WHO), and fact-checking websites.']
rob.item10_quote: De los 5 000 tuits sobre el zika mas retuiteados en el 2016, detectamos un total de 400 que contenian informacion erronea y los verificamos. De ellos, 266 contenian suficientes metadatos para reconstruir la red de difusion. [English: 'Of the 5,000 most-retweeted Zika tweets of 2016, we detected a total of 400 that contained misinformation and verified them. Of these, 266 contained enough metadata to reconstruct the dissemination network.']
